On November 17 and 18, in Jena, the conference "Academic on Demand" took place on work and organization in education. Various initiatives had followed the invitation of the FAU Jena's education section to discuss problems and strategies over the weekend in the organization of educational workers at universities and educational institutions. In the end, they agreed to continue the exchange and repeat the conference next year. The conference was attended by a total of about 30 people representing different organizations and initiatives from all over Germany:

the educational sections of the FAU Jena, Dresden and Berlin

the initiative for a student collective agreement at the Berlin Unis (TV Stud III)

the unter_bau-Hochschulgewerkschaft of the Goethe University from Frankfurt / Main

the initiative to found a basic trade union at the University of Applied Sciences in Frankfurt / Main

the initiative UniKassel unlimited

the Assistant Initiative in Marburg

the Network for Good Work in Science (NGAWiss) from Berlin

the Lecturer Initiative from Thuringia

After a large round of introductions, participants exchanged small-scale workshops on practical union organizing issues. The education section of the FAU Jena shared its experience on the practical and legal enforcement of the individual demands of student workers. The TV Stud Initiative reported on the strike movement in Berlin and talked in particular about the difficulties of participating as a radical minority organization in such a broad movement and working with the DGB unions. UniKassel open-ended presented the campaign for a cross-group, comprehensive release and unter_bau his organizing and organizing concept. Recently, the FAU Dresden reported on the organization under precarious honorary forces in educational institutions. The final round highlighted on several occasions how important and helpful was the exchange of workplace practice and trade union strategies.

An evening event on major labor disputes at universities dealt with the strike movement of student assistants in Berlin in the first half of 2018 and the two-week strike at Polish universities in mid-2018. Students there together with university employees protested against the authoritarian-neo-liberal university reform of the new government. The lecture was held by a comrade of the new section of the IP at the Warsaw University, a center of the protest movement. The IP, Polish for Workers' Initiative, is a syndicalist union and has made a name for itself in Germany in particular through the organization of Amazon workers at the Polish locations. The IP works very closely with the FAU and has been part of the "International Confederation of Workers" since May 2018.

Many discussions focused on the basic trade union model, as represented by the FAU for a long time, and how it has been successfully implemented since 2016 by the unter_bau university trade union at the Goethe University in Frankfurt / Main. Another focus of the discussions was the importance of a systematic organization of colleagues and long-term trade union strategies.

The conference also covered ongoing struggles in the education sector. The participants signed a letter of claim by the Freie Lehrzent Berlin against the introduction of monitoring and repression mechanisms in the German courses for refugees. In addition, attention was drawn to the strike and the labor disputes of the education workers and ver.di of the Anne Frank Center in Berlin. At the end of the conference, everyone took a picture together and sent their colleagues solidary greetings.

In addition to a critical evaluation of the conference, the final round dealt with prospects for the next step. For most, it was important to make better use of existing communication channels and networks, whether trade union or NGA, to exchange views, but also to request practical support in acute labor disputes.
